cohort: The study included 10,869 singleton pregnancies from a multi-ethnic population, who booked at less than 20 weeks' gestation between January 2017 and December 2018 in Counties Manukau Health, South Auckland, New Zealand.
finding: Nearly two-thirds of women with a booking HbA1c of 41-49 mmol/mol developed GDM and experienced multiple other perinatal complications, including LGA babies, pre-eclampsia, preterm births, and perinatal deaths, compared to women with HbA1c <=40 mmol/mol.
mod_finding: Women with booking HbA1c 41-49 mmol/mol had significantly higher rates of caesarean sections compared to those with normal HbA1c.
